Current monitoring methods for molecular contamination do onlyallow a limited representativeness with regards to the actual levels deposited on sensitive surfaces.Indeed, molecular contamination witnesses can almost never be placed close enough to the sensitive surfaces (for accessibility precautionary reasons) and cannot provide constant monitoring due to the incompatibility with some of the testing environments. Besides, measurements are performed periodically in laboratory environment and only provide punctual values, typically on monthly basis. For all these reasons, contamination measurements can only be taken as estimateand hypotheses are needed inorder to evaluate the levels on sensitive surfaces. This situationbecomes critical for highly sensitive items and clearly the morestringent are the requirements, thehigher risks are undertaken.Having the capability to perform in-situ real-time monitoring of the molecular contaminationdeposited on sensitive surfaces will allow to determine the actual contamination levels and to identify which phases are the most critical. Such a technology will contribute to ensure that the instrument performance will be met and will provide the capability to quickly implement mitigation actions if contamination levels increase unexpectedly. In addition, the use of this technology can be extended in flight. Operation in-flight will allow the optimization of the commissioning anddecontamination phases, thus ensuring optimal performances while maximizing instrumentavailability during the mission.Currently, two technologies are considered for the development of such a sensor, either based onOptical Micro-Electro-Mechanical-System or on micro-wave transduction.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Design definition considering the operational constraints- Manufacturingof breadboard to experimentally assess the suitability of the selected technology and its robustness against typical environment- Definition of a test plan and implementation of the associated test campaign laboratoryenvironment to determine the evaluated system performance- Identification of the required steps to manufacture a qualification unit for in-flight operationProcurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs).
